Source: https://codeload.github.com/knik0/faad2/zip/refs/tags/2.11.4
Archive SHA-256: f4d3630ffdbf17ef17e358007c91d6b51e487de0771dd2d3b3e994d4f0ad81ff
Tag: 2.11.4
Scope: decoder C sources and headers, downloaded during CMake configuration.
The Git repository retains COPYING, AUTHORS and this origin/modification record.
cmake/faad2.cmake verifies the archive SHA-256 and adapts a build-local copy.
Release source archives include the upstream decoder sources under source/.
License: GPL-2.0-or-later; see COPYING and the original per-file notices.
Code from FAAD2 is copyright (c) Nero AG, www.nero.com
Local modifications (TTPlayer Rebuild, 2026-09-22):
- include/neaacdec.h: FAAD_STATIC disables dllexport for static embedding in ttp_aac.
  It does not change the calling convention or public decoder data structures.
- libfaad/common.h: rename the MSVC inline lrintf helper to faad_lrintf to avoid a
  collision with the modern compiler's intrinsic. Keep the original x87 body.
  Include CRT math declarations before the alias so XP UCRT prototypes are
  not renamed to the private helper.
Build: x86, floating-point output, APPLY_DRC=1, /O1 /Ob2 /Os /GL,
       /fp:precise /arch:SSE2, VC-LTL 5.3.1 and YY-Thunks 1.2.2.
The wrapper derives original NeAACDecInit2's additional frame-length result
from AudioSpecificConfig, without changing the public upstream decoder ABI.
PCM validation uses the 2.11.4 baseline; it is not bit-identical to FAAD2 2.7.

Local compatibility fixes (TTPlayer Rebuild, 2026-10-29):
cmake/faad2_compat.cmake applies checked replacements to the copied build sources;
the pinned upstream archive and shared download cache are never changed.
- libfaad/syntax.c: limit the two ID_FIL/SBR look-aheads to ordinary, non-ER
  raw_data_block syntax. ER AAC's fixed channel-element sequence must not parse
  access-unit tail bits as an ordinary fill_element. This fixes AAC LD reporting
  bytesconsumed beyond the packet boundary; the wrapper's bounds check remains.
- libfaad/common.c, common.h and tns.c: use the LD TNS bandwidth limits from
  ISO/IEC 14496-3:2009 section 4.6.17.2.5, tables 4.172/4.173, including the
  different 480/512-sample limits. Pass frame length through the private helper.
  The public FAAD ABI is unchanged. The FATE er_ad6000np_44.s16 regression file
  and independent FFmpeg decoding corroborate the corrected LD output; the
  previous LC/Main/HE/LTP regression PCM remains the reference for those modes.
- libfaad/mp4.c: retain explicit 24-bit ASC frequencies and normalize them only
  when exactly equal to an existing supported frequency-table entry. SBR output
  also retains exact doubles of supported core rates (for example 192 kHz from
  a 96 kHz core), including the sync-extension form. Reject
  missing SBR presence/rate bits rather than interpreting zero-filled bits as
  a complete configuration. Unsupported arbitrary rates are not rounded.
The LD correction intentionally changes output from the original FAAD2 2.7
implementation; it is a format-correctness fix, not a bit-exact old-decoder mode.

Local native-rate extension (TTPlayer Rebuild, 2026-10-29, p4):
cmake/faad2_rates_compat.cmake applies checked build-copy replacements after the
earlier compatibility patch. Add index 12 / 7350 Hz to core sample-rate,
prediction and spectral-band tables. The 7350 Hz core uses the standard 8 kHz
band geometry while retaining its actual output rate. Do not implicitly double
this newly supported rate. Previously supported low-rate upsampling is unchanged.
Explicit and in-band SBR at 7350/14700 Hz remain rejected until their frequency
tables and synthesis have independent validation; LD at index 12 is unsupported.
The fixed upstream archive, public ABI and separate source/license distribution
are unchanged. See docs for independent PCM comparisons and remaining limits.

Local AAC completion (TTPlayer Rebuild, 2026-10-30):
- cmake/faad2_frequency_compat.cmake preserves an explicit core clock separately
  from the ISO spectral-table family. No rounding of the exposed output rate.
- cmake/faad2_ld_compat.cmake removes LD's inappropriate implicit SBR guess,
  selects the nearest defined LD table family and corrects both forward radix-5
  FFT branches used by LD480 and LTP960 prediction transforms.
- cmake/faad2_coupling_compat.cmake and src/faad_coupling implement Main/LC
  coupling at all three coupling points, checked gains/routing, per-decoder state
  and DRC handling. Main prediction now precedes intensity stereo as required.
- cmake/faad2_ssr_compat.cmake and faad2_ssr_*.c restore complete SSR gain control,
  per-band filterbank and IPQF history. SSR960 is rejected; a dormant upstream
  guard is corrected so enabling SSR does not incorrectly reject LTP960.
  The gain equations were cross-checked with the MIT-licensed reference listed
  in ../SSR_REFERENCE_NOTICE.txt; that notice accompanies the source archive.
- cmake/faad2_channel_compat.cmake activates valid ADTS channel-configuration-zero
  PCEs and separates the SCE/LFE element-tag maps. These are private decoder
  structure changes; the plugin public factory and method layouts are unchanged.
The earlier p3/p4 rate/LD limitations above describe those historical builds.
See docs/CORE_CLOCK_PCE_RESET_20261030.md, CCE_IMPLEMENTATION_20261030.md,
SSR_IMPLEMENTATION_20261030.md and LD_VALIDATION_20261030.md for current tested
scope, independent references and explicit unsupported combinations.
All adaptations still apply only to checked build-tree copies of FAAD2 2.11.4.
Local LTP/CCE follow-up (TTPlayer Rebuild, 2026-10-30p1):
- cmake/faad2_ltp_drc_compat.cmake preserves pre-DRC LTP history with a
  separately allocated unscaled overlap, only after DRC first affects a channel.
  Subsequent output gain/exclusion changes cannot feed back into prediction.
- cmake/faad2_coupling_compat.cmake and src/faad_coupling also support independent
  LTP coupling, updating both source and target prediction histories before
  time-domain mixing. Repeated targets within one CCE are rejected, while
  distinct SCE/CPE namespaces remain valid. SSR CCE and dependent LTP CCE stay
  rejected according to their normative tool restrictions.
See docs/LTP_DRC_VALIDATION_20261030P1.md and CCE_LTP_COMPATIBILITY_20261030P1.md
for independent references, actual predicting streams and remaining limits.
No additional runtime library or change to the public plugin ABI is introduced.
